comments.text:
Simulation theory seems more and more likely the more you research quantum physics and the general foundation of the universe.

Suddenly everything just existed from one point in time and space, then exploded outwards, and is continuing to expand? What about the smallest possible segments of both matter and time? Planck length? Planck time? How electrons will change how they interact with their environment, purely by whether they're being observed/measured or not? Wave-particle duality, double-slit experiment type stuff.

This also gets paradoxical with the nesting doll issue. If we're in a simulation, is the world outside of our simulation also simulated? If so, how far does it go until base-reality?
